name: VoiceX – Text to Speech Reader
author: WPXERO

sections.description:
VoiceX turns every WordPress post into audio in one click. Visitors press Listen and hear the article read aloud in the most natural voice their device has. It is free text to speech with no API key, no account and no per-character fees. Activate it and the player is already live on your posts.

Why add text to speech to your site?

Not every visitor wants to read. Some are on a phone, commuting, cooking or working out. Some have low vision, dyslexia or tired eyes, or are reading in a second language. A Listen button lets all of them take in your full article instead of skimming it or leaving.

VoiceX works well for:

  • Blogs and magazines – give long reads an audio version without recording anything.
  • News sites – let readers catch up hands-free.
  • Recipe and how-to sites – visitors listen while their hands are busy.
  • Schools, courses and documentation – support learners who understand better by listening.
  • Online stores – read product descriptions aloud (with VoiceX Pro).

How does VoiceX work?

  1. Activate VoiceX. A Listen player appears on your single posts straight away. No setup is needed.
  2. A visitor presses Listen. Their browser reads the title and the article, one sentence at a time, in the most natural voice their device has for your language.
  3. They stay in control. Pause, resume from the last word, stop, and (if you allow it) pick a voice and a speed.

Speech uses the browser’s built-in Web Speech API, so it runs on the visitor’s own device. Nothing is uploaded and nothing is billed.

Free features

  • Ready in seconds – the player appears on single posts as soon as the plugin is active. Turn on pages and custom post types with one checkbox.
  • Unlimited and free – no usage caps, no character limits, no account.
  • Natural voices first – VoiceX picks the most natural-sounding voice on each device (neural and online voices first) and never uses novelty voices. Set a preferred voice, speed and pitch if you like.
  • Accessible player – real buttons with visible focus, full keyboard support, screen reader announcements and 44 px touch targets.
  • Play, pause, resume and stop, with optional voice and speed menus for visitors. Their choice is remembered in their own browser.
  • Two layouts – Standard (controls in a panel) or Button only (a single Listen button).
  • Place it anywhere – automatically before or after the content, or by hand with the VoiceX Player block, the [wpxero_text_to_speech] shortcode or the Elementor widget. The shortcode also works in Divi, Bricks and other page builders.
  • Per-post control – hide the automatic player on any post from the block editor panel or the classic editor box.
  • Reads only the article – skips scripts, menus, forms, hidden elements and the player itself. The title can be read first.
  • Reliable on long articles – reads one sentence at a time so browsers don’t stop part-way, and pauses cleanly when a phone locks or the tab goes to the background.
  • Multilingual – reads any language the visitor’s device has a voice for. With Polylang or WPML, each post is read in its own language.
  • Live preview – a setup checklist and a preview that plays your unsaved changes.
  • Fast and cache-friendly – one small script and stylesheet, loaded only on pages with a player. React runs only in the admin screen.
  • Private by design – no tracking, no cookies and no visitor data on your server.
  • Translation-ready – every interface string can be translated.

VoiceX Pro: the same studio voice for every visitor

Browser voices are free, but they sound different on every device. VoiceX Pro gives every visitor the same natural AI voice and turns your posts into an audio channel. It adds sections to the same VoiceX screen; nothing to migrate.

  • Natural AI voices – connect your own OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Google Cloud or Microsoft Azure account. Each post is recorded once and played from your site, on any device and even with the screen locked. Your provider bills you directly, with no extra per-character fee from us.
  • Podcast feed – publish your recordings as a podcast for Apple Podcasts and Spotify.
  • Listening stats – plays and listens to the end for each post, counted on your site without cookies.
  • Read-along highlighting – the sentence (and, where the voice supports it, the word) being read is highlighted.
  • Listen to a selection – visitors select a passage and hear just that part.
  • Nine more player designs – Studio (a podcast card with cover art, seek bar and skip buttons), Capsule, Editorial, Waveform, Glass, Midnight, Expanded, Compact and Minimal, with your own colours and labels, plus a floating mini player.
  • Content rules – place the player after any paragraph, choose what is read, and skip posts by category, tag or length.
  • WooCommerce product pages, per-post settings and settings import/export.

See every Pro feature or compare plans and pricing. You can also open VoiceX › Pricing in your dashboard.

Shortcode

[wpxero_text_to_speech]

Optional attributes:

  • layout – standard or button (extensions may add more)
  • title – yes or no: read the post title first
  • lang – a language code such as en-GB
  • rate – speed from 0.5 to 2

Example: [wpxero_text_to_speech layout="button" title="no" rate="1.25"]. Invalid values are ignored and the settings are used instead. A post that contains the block or shortcode does not also get the automatic player.

Browser support and limitations

Free voices, languages and quality depend on the visitor’s operating system and browser, so the same page can sound different on different devices. Some in-app and privacy-focused browsers have no speech support; the player then says so instead of showing controls that do nothing. Some browsers stop speaking when the tab is in the background or the screen locks; VoiceX then pauses at the last word so the visitor can resume.

Some browser vendors provide online voices that process text on their own servers. That is a browser feature outside the plugin’s control.

VoiceX helps visitors who prefer to listen. It is not a screen reader, and it does not by itself make a site conform to WCAG or any other accessibility standard.

External services

The player itself uses no external service. The plugin includes the Freemius SDK for two purposes:

  • Optional opt-in – after activation, Freemius asks the administrator to opt in (“Allow & Continue”) or “Skip”. Nothing is sent unless they opt in, there or later from the VoiceX Overview screen. If they do, Freemius receives the administrator’s name and email address, the site address, the WordPress, PHP and plugin versions and, if allowed, the list of plugins and themes, to send security and feature-update notices and non-sensitive diagnostics. You can opt out at any time from the plugin’s row on the Plugins screen.
  • VoiceX Pro licensing – buying, activating and updating VoiceX Pro happens through Freemius.

When you deactivate the plugin you may answer an optional one-question survey; the answer is sent to Freemius only if you submit it. See the Freemius terms of service and privacy policy. Your visitors’ data is never sent.

Credits

VoiceX bundles the following third-party code and assets:

  • Freemius WordPress SDK by Freemius, GPL-3.0-or-later (licensing and the optional opt-in).
  • Figtree font by Erik Kennedy, SIL Open Font License 1.1.
  • Geist Mono font by Vercel, SIL Open Font License 1.1.
  • Material Symbols icons by Google, Apache License 2.0.
sections.installation:
1. In your dashboard, go to Plugins › Add New, search for VoiceX, then install and activate it. Or upload the ZIP file there.
  2. You land on the VoiceX Overview, with a live preview of the player. Press Listen to try it.
  3. Open any single post: the player is already shown before the content.
  4. Optional: under VoiceX, choose content types, placement, layout, voice and speed.
sections.faq:
How do I add text to speech to WordPress for free?

Install and activate VoiceX. A Listen button appears on your single posts automatically, and visitors hear the article read aloud in their browser’s own voices. There is no API key, account or usage fee.

Is VoiceX really free?

Yes. The text to speech player, automatic and manual placement, both layouts, voice and speed settings and the accessible controls are free, with no usage limits. VoiceX Pro is an optional paid add-on for AI voices, a podcast feed, stats and more player designs.

Do I need an API key or a paid speech service?

No. VoiceX uses the speech voices built into each visitor’s browser and device. There is nothing to sign up for. An API key is only needed if you choose AI voices with VoiceX Pro.

How do I add a “Listen” button to my WordPress posts?

Activate VoiceX: the button appears on single posts automatically. To place it somewhere specific, add the VoiceX Player block, the [wpxero_text_to_speech] shortcode or the Elementor widget where it should appear.

How do I add text to speech to pages or custom post types?

Go to VoiceX › General and tick the content types under Content types. You can also place the block or shortcode on any page by hand.

Does it work on iPhone and Android?

Yes. VoiceX works in the browsers on iPhone, iPad and Android that support speech, including Safari and Chrome, with 44 px touch targets. Some phones stop speech when the screen locks; VoiceX then pauses so the visitor can resume. With VoiceX Pro AI voices, playback continues with the screen locked.

Which languages are supported?

Any language for which the visitor’s device has a voice. The reading language defaults to your site language; change it under Voice and playback, per player with the shortcode’s lang attribute, or let Polylang or WPML set it for each post.

Which voice will visitors hear?

The preferred voice set under Voice and playback, if their device has it. Otherwise the most natural-sounding voice for the reading language on their device (neural and online voices first; novelty voices are never picked), then the best voice in the device’s own language. Voices differ between devices; VoiceX Pro can give every visitor the same AI voice.

Can I use AI voices such as OpenAI or ElevenLabs?

Yes, with VoiceX Pro. Connect your own OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Google Cloud or Microsoft Azure account; each post is recorded once and every visitor hears the same natural voice. Your provider bills you directly, with no extra per-character fee.

Can I turn my blog posts into a podcast?

Yes, with VoiceX Pro. It records your posts with an AI voice and publishes them as a podcast feed you can submit to Apple Podcasts and Spotify.

Will it slow down my site?

No. The player is one small script and stylesheet, loaded only on pages that show it, and the speech runs in the visitor’s browser. It works with page caching.

Does text to speech help SEO?

Text to speech is not a ranking factor by itself. VoiceX never changes your article text, loads its files only on pages with a player and works with caching, so it does not get in the way of page speed or indexing. Its benefit is for your readers: more ways to take in your content.

Does it work with WooCommerce, Elementor, Divi or the classic editor?

Yes. Use the Elementor widget, or the shortcode in Divi, Bricks and other builders, and the VoiceX box in the classic editor. The player on WooCommerce product pages is part of VoiceX Pro.

Can visitors choose the voice and speed?

Yes, if you allow it under Player › Visitor controls. Their choice is remembered in their own browser only.

How do I hide the player on one post?

In the block editor, open the VoiceX panel in the post sidebar and turn off Show the automatic player. In the classic editor, untick it in the VoiceX box.

Does the plugin collect or send personal data?

Not about your visitors: the player sets no cookies, makes no external requests and stores nothing about them on your server. A visitor’s voice and speed choice is kept in their own browser. For the site administrator, the only data sharing is the optional Freemius opt-in described under External services.

Is VoiceX a screen reader? Does it make my site accessible?

No to both. Screen reader users keep using their own screen reader; VoiceX is for everyone who prefers to listen. It supports your accessibility work but does not by itself make a site meet WCAG or any law.

The player says “There is no text to read here”

The automatic player reads the element it is placed in. Some themes put the article text somewhere else; place the block or shortcode inside the content instead.

What happens without JavaScript or speech support?

The player stays hidden until its script runs, so there are no buttons that do nothing. In browsers without speech support the player says so.

What happens to my settings when I deactivate or delete the plugin?

They are kept, so you can reactivate later. To remove them when deleting the plugin, turn on Delete settings when the plugin is deleted under General.

Where is the source code?

The compiled files in build/ are built from the source at github.com/WPXERO/wpxero-text-to-speech (npm install && npm run build).
sections.changelog:
1.0.1 – November 21, 2026

  • Fix: sentences are no longer cut after abbreviations such as “Dr.”, “St.” or an initial, so the voice reads “Dr. Smith” without a pause in the middle.
  • Improved: voice menus no longer repeat the language when the voice name already includes it.
  • Improved: clearer wording for the player layouts and the privacy notes in Help.
  • Improved: the save bar stays out of the way on Overview and Help until you have changes to save.
  • Changed: after activation, the standard Freemius opt-in screen asks whether to share basic site data (Allow & Continue) or Skip, as in our other plugins.

1.0.0 – November 7, 2026

  • First release: a free text to speech Listen player for posts, pages and custom post types.
  • Automatic placement before or after the content, the VoiceX Player block, a shortcode and an Elementor widget.
  • Natural voice selection that never uses novelty voices, with optional visitor voice and speed choices.
  • Accessible controls, sentence-by-sentence reading and clean pausing on mobile.
  • Polylang and WPML support, a classic editor box and a settings screen with a live preview.
